title: Preflight & Rollback Runbook for VPC Edge Cases
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures preflight checks, upgrade gating, and a conservative rollback plan for VPC/on‑prem private deployments where subtle network and Terraform ordering issues have caused silent failures. Target audience: SREs and private-deploy engineers running installs, upgrades, or emergency rollbacks for customer VPC and air‑gapped stacks.

Scope and motivation:
- Covers preflight checks that catch common failure classes we repeatedly see in customer installs: DNS split‑horizon issues, route propagation delays, KMS/HSM permission gaps, provider/plugin version drift, and Terraform race conditions.
- Provides a stepwise upgrade flow with instrumentation gates and a minimal-impact rollback path.
- Includes a compact smoke verification checklist (fast commands + expected pass/fail signals) intended to be runnable from the support laptop or bastion host.

Quick index (jump targets):
- Preconditions and privileges required
- Network/DNS/Route sanity checks
- Terraform module/version notes and gotchas
- Upgrade flow (canary -> partial -> full) + gating metrics
- Rollback decision matrix and safe commands
- Runtime smoke tests and expected artifacts
- Failure patterns and triage tips
- Short scripts / one‑liners to run during incident
- Postmortem checkpoints and TODOs

Prerequisites (what to have open before starting):
- Terminal with MFA to customer bastion (sudo, kubeconfig and aws/gcloud creds where applicable)
- Access to customer KMS console / HSM admin (if used)
- Terraform state access (S3/GCS/remote backend) + state locking working
- Observation dashboards: per-node CPU/GPU, per-route token latency, model-serving traces, system logs aggregator (ELK/Cloudwatch)
- Ticket/Change request ID to link any manual approvals

Preflight checklist (run these before terraform apply or upgrade):
1) Confirm network reachability and MTU
   - From bastion: traceroute to each node IP, and to private control plane endpoints. Expect <5 hops inside VPC; if UDP traceroute blocked, use tcping on 443.
   - MTU mismatches cause large payload drop for gRPC large batches: ip link show; look for mismatches between host and overlay (e.g. host eth0 1500 vs docker0 1450).

2) DNS and split‑horizon
   - Verify internal DNS resolves the private control plane and KMS endpoints: dig +short control-plane.internal.customer.local
   - Check time to resolve and TTL; long negative caching (>300s) indicates upstream resolver issues.

3) Route tables and BGP/propagation windows
   - For VPN/Transit gateways verify route propagation has completed. On AWS, check route table propagation; on-prem BGP flaps may show short lived withdraws.
   - If recent networking changes: wait 2x propagation window before proceeding (typical: 2–5 min for cloud, 15–30 min for BGP changes).

4) KMS/HSM key policy and grant test
   - Try an encrypt/decrypt round trip using the key to be used by runtime (CLI): aws kms encrypt --key-id <key> --plaintext 'test' ... then decrypt. Fail here? Stop.

5) Node preflight: OS, drivers, container runtime
   - Kernel & nvidia driver: uname -r; nvidia-smi (expect driver version consistent with runtime).
   - Container runtime: containerd/podman/docker health (systemctl status containerd).
   - GPU visible inside a container: docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.7-base nvidia-smi

6) Terraform backend & locking
   - Confirm remote state can be read and lock can be acquired: terraform init && terraform plan -target=module.bootstrap
   - If using S3 backend ensure bucket lifecycle hasn’t archived state files; verify encryption/permissions.

Terraform module and version notes (recent gotchas we've observed):
- provider.aws v4->v5: subtle resource renames cause resource replacement if provider aliasing omitted. Pin provider to range = ">=4.50, <5.0" for known-stable stacks.
- module.private_network: recent change (v2.3.1) added a dependency on route_attachment; if you bump module there may be a transient taint ordering between attachment and ec2 instance creation. Use terraform plan -refresh=true and inspect for implicit replaces.
- Remote-exec provisioners that assume ssh availability often race with instance boot scripts (cloud-init). Use a null_resource with explicit depends_on or a local-exec step in operator workflow instead of remote-exec in module.
- State drift: customers who manually change security groups cause repeated module churn. Add a note in the preflight to compare live SGs vs terraform plan before apply.

Upgrade plan (conservative):
- Stage A — Canary (single node / single availability zone): apply to 1 node, wait for green health for 20–30 min under low synthetic traffic.
- Gate 1 — Observability: no increase in 5xx, GPU memory OOMs, sustained CPU >85% for model-container over 5min, no restart storms.
- Stage B — Partial (20–30% of capacity across zones): roll additional nodes while monitoring end-to-end latency and sample outputs (automated prompt set).
- Gate 2 — Data plane & correctness: embedding similarity diffs within tolerance, no regression alarms triggered in quality monitoring (Redwood Optimize signals).
- Stage C — Full: rest of fleet; run final KV cache warmup and latency-benchmarking.

Gating metrics and thresholds (suggested):
- Error rate: 5xx increase >0.5% absolute over baseline for 10 minutes -> pause rollout.
- Tail latency: p99 increase >25% absolute -> pause.
- GPU OOMs: any OOM -> immediately pause and roll back canary.
- Model output regression: 5% of sample prompts show >threshold change in similarity or token divergence -> investigate before proceeding.

Rollback decision matrix (simple):
- If gating metric exceeded in Canary -> rollback to previous group immediately.
- If partial stage but <10% user impact and transient -> pause and run deeper triage for 15–30 minutes. If no fix, rollback.
- If full stage and market impacting -> emergency rollback and open incident.

Safe rollback commands (Terraform-friendly):
- If you still have the previous plan: terraform apply "previous-plan.tfplan"
- If not, targeted rollback: terraform state list | grep module.node; terraform apply -target=module.node[0] --refresh=false (use sparingly: ensures instance group replaced without touching independent infra).
- If module-level drift caused resource delete/replace, prefer to restore state file from remote backend snapshot rather than manual state edits.

Runtime smoke checks (quick, indexable):
1) Health endpoints
   - curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/healthz -> OK expected.
   - curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/metrics | head -n 20 -> look for model_loaded 1 and kv_cache_entries > 0.

\2) Basic inference sanity (local run)
   - Send small prompt to local runtime (curl POST); expect 200 and tokens returned within 2s for tiny model. Sample: POST /v1/generate {"input":"hello"} -> response tokens array non-empty.

3) KV cache warmup test
   - Run a synthetic session to prime KV and verify subsequent latency drop: run 10 sequential similar prompts and observe median latency decreases by >=20%.

4) GPU and memory checks
   - dmesg | grep -i oom or journalctl -u inference-runtime | grep OOM -> any occurrence is fatal for this upgrade.
   - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 2 (watch for memory climbing steadily).

5) Batching & throughput check
   - Run the internal micro-benchmark script (scripts/bench/batch_test.sh) at intended concurrency and verify RPS within 10% of baseline.

Common failure patterns and triage notes (patterns we've repeatedly hit):
- Problem: Terraform apply hangs on route attachment
  - Symptom: apply waits then times out, state shows partial attachment.
  - Hypothesis: underlying cloud API rate limit / propagation delay.
  - Quick triage: aws ec2 describe-route-tables for route status; check cloud provider events. If propagation pending, wait 10–15 minutes or re-run apply with -refresh=true.

- Problem: KMS decrypt failure on startup only in canary nodes
  - Symptom: runtime logs show key not found or AccessDenied for kms:Decrypt.
  - Triage: validate that grant on key includes the IAM role used by instance profile. Run temporary encrypt/decrypt using instance credentials to replicate.

- Problem: Model server restarts with CUDA init errors
  - Symptom: inference container crash loop with cudaErrorUnknown
  - Triage: check driver/runtime mismatch: nvidia-smi on host vs libcudnn/cuda in container. Confirm container image tag matches host driver compatibility matrix. If mismatch, revert image to prior tag or schedule host driver upgrade outside of traffic window.

Incident one-liners and small scripts (can paste and run from bastion):
- Quick health dump for a node (single command):
  HOST=10.0.1.23; ssh ubuntu@$HOST "sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime --no-pager --since '5 minutes ago' | tail -n 200; docker ps --filter name=inference -q | xargs -r docker logs --tail 200"

- Terraform dry-check with state lock verification:
  terraform init -backend-config="bucket=customer-state" && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan | jq '.resource_changes[] | {type: .type, change: .change.actions}'

- Snapshot remote state (safe backup to avoid state loss during emergency):
  aws s3 cp s3://customer-state/terraform.tfstate ./tfstate-snapshot-$(date +%F-%H%M).backup

Logs and places to look (priority order):
1) inference-runtime service logs (systemd or container logs)
2) kubelet/containerd logs if using k8s
3) /var/log/cloud-init-output.log and system journal for boot issues
4) cloud provider events (console) and route table / VPC flow logs for packet drops

Escalation matrix (who to ping quickly):
- First 10 minutes: eng-private-deployments on call -> @Liam Chen, then @Aisha Patel if network related -> @NetInfra on-call (if transit/gateway BGP).
- KMS/HSM: @Mariana Gomez -> security infra on-call.
- If it's GPU/driver: @Omar Khan (serving-runtime).

Post-rollback checklist (after successful rollback):
- Verify all nodes report healthy in control plane and that any restart counts are back to baseline.
- Create a postmortem stub in Confluence and link the change ID and plan used.
- If rollback used state restore from backup, note exact snapshot name and time in postmortem.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Consider adding an automated preflight that verifies KMS grants using the instance-role temp creds (small lambda or script).
- We still see intermittent route-propagation timing on MSP customer networks; need a longer propagation wait default for BGP-linked installs.
- TODO: formalize a terraform safe-apply wrapper that does a plan, verifies diff for security groups, and requires a manual approval if SG changes are detected.

References and helpful commands (copyable):
- health: curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/healthz || echo FAIL
- metrics peek: curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/metrics | egrep 'model_loaded|kv_cache_entries' | head -n 10
- quick encrypt test (aws): aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/redwood-deploy-test --plaintext fileb://<(echo -n "ok") --output text | awk '{print $1}'

End of runbook.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-07: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-12-15: added gating thresholds and Terraform module notes (Liam)
- 2025-02-20: added canary rollback text and one-liners (Mariana)
